title: 혼잣말, 퀴즈, 한 번 더 묻기: -나 / -게 / -고
objective: By the end, you can choose between -나(요), -게(요), and -고(요) to fit the situation (talking to yourself, giving a quiz, or adding a question), and attach each ending correctly to present and past forms, and -게(요) and -고(요) to nouns.
summary: Learn three spoken question endings: -나(요) for wondering or asking softly, -게(요) for asking someone to guess, and -고(요) for adding one more question.

task.title: Choose and write endings
task.line: Read the situation in each item first, then decide what kind of question it is: wondering, a guessing quiz, or one more question.

forms.when: Use -나 alone when you wonder about something to yourself or talk to a close friend. Use -나요 to ask someone a soft, polite question.
forms.exampleMeaning: Why hasn't my package come yet, I wonder?

forms.form: A/V-게(요)? / A/V-았/었게(요)? / N이게(요)? (after a vowel: N게(요)?)
forms.when: Use this when you already know the answer and want the listener to guess it, like a quiz.

forms.form: A/V-고(요)? / A/V-았/었고(요)? / N이고(요)? (after a vowel: N고(요)?)
forms.when: Use this to add one more question to what someone just told you. Say it with a rising tone. A falling tone makes it a statement instead.
forms.exampleMeaning: Oh, you moved? And do you like your new place?

watchOut: 지금 몇 시게요? (X) → 지금 몇 시예요? (O): Use -게요 only when you know the answer and want a guess. If you really don't know, ask a normal question.
선생님, 내일 오나? (X) → 선생님, 내일 오시나요? (O): -나 without 요 is for yourself or close friends. To older people, use -(으)시나요.
제가 어제 뭐 살게요? (X) → 제가 어제 뭐 샀게요? (O): For a guess about the past, use -았/었게요. -(으)ㄹ게요 is a promise, not a quiz.
exercises: Fill in each blank with -나, -게, or -고: ① (To yourself, looking at your empty wallet) 돈을 어디에 뒀__? ② (To a friend, hiding something behind your back) 내가 뭐 가져왔__? ③ (B already reacted to the news and now adds one more question with "And …?") A: 동생이 대학교에 합격했어요. B: 축하해요! 부모님도 많이 기뻐하시__요?
Fill in the blank with -았/었고요 (use 예약하다): A: 다음 주에 부산으로 출장 가요. B: 그래요? 호텔은 벌써 ____?
Fill in the blank with -나요 to ask a bus driver politely (use 가다): 저기요, 이 버스가 시청에 ____?
Make a guessing question with -게요: ① (Showing a friend a photo of your hometown) 제 고향이 ____? (어디) ② (Showing your new phone) 이 휴대폰 얼마 ____? 맞혀 보세요. (주다)
Each sentence has a mistake. Rewrite it correctly: ① (You really don't know the date) 오늘 며칠이게요? ② (To your manager) 부장님, 점심 드셨나?
answers: ① 뒀나 ② 가져왔게 ③ 기뻐하시고요
① 오늘 며칠이에요? ② 부장님, 점심 드셨나요? (드셨어요?)
